searchText: hey <@393119312350543872> , Was just talking to <@892053833121923094> about the latest PyTests released here: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/releases/tag/v1.0.5 Can we push the same fixtures on: ethereum/tests? We utilize it to run those tests in our pipelines. would be really great to have it 🙏 Yes, no problem, I check that everything is generated fine and publish it to the test repo And with this change (beacon roots) can start all test cancun revision. just to confirm, this update should have BlobBaseFee opcode tests. Correct? yes `+Tests for EIP-7516: BLOBBASEFEE opcode` 9/11 eip. Here https://github.com/ethereum/tests/pull/1299 Thank you 🙏 i see these but no valid calls, is that intentional or do valid calls exist in these files also? This is a question to pyspec team <@755913785620824175> <@892053833121923094> Yes, all excess_blob_gas tests do a call that use the opcode with different blob gas values on the txs its just from the file names, it seems that those are tests either before the fork, or with overflow or with no gas. so none of the file names indicate a successful usage It's on another suite, it was added to `eip4844_blobs/excess_blob_gas` tests in this PR: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/pull/294/files got it. thanks In Shanghai folder? I agree that it's kind of confusing to have this check somewhere else, it might be worth it to add more tests not to increase coverage but to make it clear that we are actually testing it It should be in cancun: - `cancun/eip4844_blobs/excess_blob_gas` - `cancun/eip7516_blobgasfee/blobgasfee_opcode` Also a test case versioning would be nice. A reference which exact case is covered in which test file. Like we tried in readme.md
